title: My World
subtitle: All About Me

project.title: My World Profile
project.description: Create a personal profile and present your world in simple English.
project.deliverable: A one-page profile or a 60–90 second spoken presentation.
successCriteria: I can describe people and places that are important to me.
I can say what I like and what I do every day.
I can present my profile using simple sentences.

objectives: Introduce yourself and ask for basic personal information.
Describe family, friends and familiar places.
Use be, have got, possessive adjectives and there is/are.
Talk about likes, routines and everyday life.
Create and present a short personal profile.

vocabulary.example: My family is important to me.
My school is near my home.

grammar.title: Verb be
grammar.rule: I am · You are · He/She/It is · We/They are

grammar.title: Have got
grammar.rule: I/You/We/They have got · He/She has got

grammar.title: Possessive adjectives
grammar.rule: my · your · his · her · our · their

grammar.title: There is / There are
grammar.rule: There is + one thing · There are + two or more things
examples: There is a desk in my room.
There are two parks near my home.

grammar.title: Present Simple: likes and routines
grammar.rule: I like / I play / I go · He likes / He plays / He goes

screens.title: Welcome to My World
screens.body: Every person has a world: people, places, interests and everyday moments. Let’s discover yours — and learn how to talk about it in English.
screens.prompt: Your final mission is to create a My World Profile. Each activity will help you build one part of it.

screens.title: Look. Think. Connect.
screens.body: Look at the three photographs. What connects them? Choose the ideas that come to your mind, then make a guess about our topic.
screens.question: What can connect people, places and interests?
screens.feedback: Think about the people around you, the places you know and the things you enjoy. They are all part of your world.

screens.title: Your mission
screens.body: Create a personal profile in English. Imagine you are introducing yourself to a new international friend.
steps: Describe people who are important to you.
Talk about your home and hometown.
Share your interests and daily routine.

screens.title: Words for your world
screens.body: Explore the key words. Read each example aloud and think of a true sentence about your own life.

screens.title: Vocabulary check
screens.body: Choose the best word to complete each sentence.

questions.q: My ___ is Anna. Nice to meet you.
questions.why: We use name to say what a person is called.
Live means to have your home in a place.
Favourite means the one you like most.

screens.title: Grammar Lab 1 · Verb be
screens.body: Use be to give basic information and describe people and places.

screens.title: Build a sentence
screens.body: Choose the correct form of be.

questions.why: Use is with he, she and it.

screens.title: Reading · Meet Mia
screens.body: Read Mia’s profile. Notice how she introduces herself and describes her world.
screens.text: Hi! My name is Mia and I’m 13. I live in a small town near the sea. I’ve got one brother and a friendly dog called Max. My best friend is Lily. We are in the same class. I like drawing and listening to music. At weekends, I usually ride my bike with Lily. There is a lovely park near my house.

options: In a small town near the sea

questions.q: What does Mia do at weekends?

screens.title: Grammar Lab 2 · Have got
screens.body: Use have got to talk about family members, pets and possessions.

screens.title: My people
screens.body: Complete the sentences with have got, has got, my or her.

items.hint: Use a possessive adjective before a noun.

screens.title: Grammar Lab 3 · There is / There are
screens.body: Describe a room, a home or a place in your town.

questions.why: Use There is with one thing.
Use There are with plural nouns.

screens.title: Listening · A new friend
screens.body: Listen to the short introduction. Then answer the questions. If audio is unavailable, use the transcript toggle.
screens.audioText: Hello! I'm Ben. I'm twelve years old and I live in Bristol. I've got a big family: two sisters and one brother. I love skateboarding and I play basketball after school. My favourite place is the park near my home.

questions.q: How many sisters has Ben got?
What does Ben do after school?

screens.title: Project Workshop · Build your profile
screens.body: Use the prompts to create the first version of your My World Profile. You can edit it before the final presentation.

fields.label: My name and age
fields.placeholder: My name is ... I am ... years old.

fields.label: People important to me
fields.placeholder: I have got ... My best friend is ...

screens.title: Challenge · Your new classmate
screens.body: A new student joins your class. They do not know anyone yet. Help them feel welcome.
screens.scenario: You have one minute to introduce yourself and ask two friendly questions.
prompts: Have you got any brothers or sisters?

screens.title: Present your world
screens.body: Bring your profile together. Read it aloud or record a 60–90 second presentation. Use the checklist before you finish.
checklist: I described at least one person.

screens.title: Look back · What can you do now?
screens.body: Think about your progress. Honest reflection helps you choose the next step.
questions: I can introduce myself in English.
I can describe people and places.
I can talk about my interests and routine.
I can present my My World Profile.

screens.title: Mission complete!
screens.body: You have built your first English project. Your My World Profile is the starting point for real communication. Keep it — you can improve it as your English grows.
